en: The Theravāda Vinaya:
Bhikkhunīvibhaṅga,
Pācittiyakaṇḍa
Chattupāhanavagga 88.
The Training Rule on Perfumes and Cosmetics.
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, the group-of-six bhikkhunīs were bathing with scents and ointments.
People complained, grumbled, and became indignant, saying:
"How can these bhikkhunīs bathe with scents and ointments? They are just like householders who indulge in sensual pleasures!"
The bhikkhunīs heard those people grumbling, complaining, and criticizing.
Those bhikkhunīs who were of few desires... [and so on]... they grumbled, complained, and criticized:
"How can the bhikkhunīs of the group of six bathe with scents and ointments?"... [and so on]...
“Is it true, monks, that the group-of-six bhikkhunīs bathe with scents and ointments?
“It is true, Blessed One.
The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them … [as before] …
"How indeed, monks, could the group-of-six bhikkhunīs bathe with scents and ointments?
This, monks, is neither for the inspiration of those without faith nor for the increase of the faith of those who have it...

And thus, monks, should the bhikkhunīs recite this training rule: "Whatever bhikkhunī should bathe with scents and ointments, there is an offense of expiation."* *The full rule includes the penalty clause.*
“Whatever nun should bathe with scented coloring matter, it is an offense entailing expiation.
Regarding “whatever nun”:
whoever such a one... [and so forth].
"Bhikkhunī" ...
[as before] ... this is the kind of bhikkhunī intended in this context.
"Gandha" (fragrance) means:
Any kind of scent whatsoever.
"Coloring" means any kind of coloring whatsoever.
"Should bathe" means she bathes. There is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa) for the act; at the conclusion of the bathing, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
There is no offense—
On account of illness,
for one who is insane,
or for one who is a first-time offender.
The fifth training rule is concluded.
